method: All GEPS member rainfall sequences are recomputed for three uncertainty configurations. The site-transfer sensitivity shifts the required modelled RS18883 WSE by plus or minus 0.15 m. Hydrologic response uses lower, central or upper short-range delays and later-window analogue RMSE sensitivity.

uncertainty_components.meteorological: Full validated GEPS member spread through 16 days.
uncertainty_components.later_hydrologic: Each later rainfall window uses central days lost minus/plus its analogue RMSE for low/high sensitivity.
uncertainty_components.rating: The current-limb stage-discharge fit is used in every configuration; uncertainty in the provisional WSC rating is described separately and is not assigned a false probability distribution.

optimistic_sensitivity.interpretation: Higher allowable modelled WSE plus lower analogue response delays. This is a sensitivity bound, not a stated probability.

central.interpretation: Nominal 650.20 m threshold and central analogue response delays.

conservative_sensitivity.interpretation: Requires the modelled WSE to fall 0.15 m below the nominal threshold and applies upper analogue-response delays. This is a planning sensitivity bound, not a calibrated confidence interval.

planning_summary.recommended_use: Use central p50 as the working inspection forecast and conservative-sensitivity p90 as the protected schedule contingency. These bounds deliberately include more than weather spread but remain sensitivity results, not formal confidence limits.

limitations: Analogue RMSE is unavailable as formal cross-validation with only two clean training events, so fallback error magnitudes are used.
The plus/minus 0.15 m project-transfer sensitivity is an engineering working allowance, not a fitted statistical distribution.
The same current-limb WSC rating fit is used in all cases; provisional-rating error is not probabilistically quantified.
Local ponding and bearing capacity remain outside the hydrologic crossing-date calculation.
